subject: jacobian of random effect vector w.r.t. fixed effect vector.  Approximating covariance matrix of a single random effect vector.

messages.author: 0965a429193e691b
messages.subject: jacobian of random effect vector w.r.t. fixed effect vector.  Approximating covariance matrix of a single random effect vector.
parts:
Hello,

I'm interested in the most efficient way to get an approximation of the covariance matrix of a random effect vector.

Say I have several random effect vectors in a model

  PARAMETER_VECTOR( ua );
  PARAMETER_VECTOR( ub );
  PARAMETER_VECTOR( uc );

and a fixed effect vector "theta".

And I'm interested in particular in getting the variance covariance matrix for one of these, say

"ua"

Looking at the documentation of sdreport(), I see



So what I'd like is the upper left block matrix of the above.

I believe I can get the first component by using

sdreport(obj, getJointPrecision=TRUE)

and taking the inverse of the JointPrecision matrix for the submatrix containing "ua".

For the second component , is there a way to extract or output the jacobian of "ua" with respect to fixed effects "theta"  in the second part? 



Thanks in advance for any help,
Dan

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: jacobian of random effect vector w.r.t. fixed effect vector.  Approximating covariance matrix of a single random effect vector.
parts:
Hi,

I am not sure understand completely, because sdreport() would give you the covariance matrix for random effects vectors (standard deviations
for sure, but I suspect that it must be possible to extract the full covariance matrix).

However, I you want to do it "by hand", there is a closed form formula for J that involves only what you get out of model$he(), when you
turn "ua" into a fixed effect. 

Hans

messages.subject: Re: jacobian of random effect vector w.r.t. fixed effect vector.  Approximating covariance matrix of a single random effect vector.
parts:
Thanks for your reply,

and apologies for the confusion which is probably due to my limited understanding.

I am aware that sdreport() gives me the standard errors, but I was interested in the full covariance matrix because I have some correlation structure modeled in the random effects, and so am thinking that the covariances may be non-negligible. 

say
jp<-sdreport(obj,getJointPrecision=TRUE)$jointPrecision



and

solve(jp)


or

Matrix::chol2inv(Matrix::chol(jp))
  Cholmod error 'problem too large' at file ../Core/cholmod_dense.c, line 105


are too large of a problem, because for example "ub", and "uc" may be 100 times longer vectors than "ua", and "ua" is my primary interest. 


Solving the submatrix of jp
corresponding to random effect vector "ua" is really not correct, and underestimates the standard errors by a factor.

summary(sqrt(diag(solve(jp[rownames(jp)=="ua",rownames(jp)=="ua"]))) / mysdsummary[param=="ua",`Std. Error`])
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.
 0.3049  0.6619  0.7745  0.7424  0.8370  0.9319


 cor(sqrt(diag(solve(jp[rownames(jp)=="ua",rownames(jp)=="ua"]))),mysdsummary[param=="ua",`Std. Error`])
[1] 0.9590948


 
So, I'm wondering what the best approximation / easiest workaround might be.  It seems that internally the calculation has already been made by sdreport(), otherwise I wouldn't have the standard errors.

Do you think the best workaround may involve using model$he(), and calling "ua" a fixed effect, ? 

Or is there another way to output this report, without requiring a full covariance matrix for all random effects, i.e. "ub", "uc", ...?

Thanks very much,
Dan
